messages.subject: CAR
parts:
Hello,

I have fitted the following CAR model on a couple of data sets in INLA:

Y_i = Intercept + b * X_i + u_i + eps_i

with:

eps_i ~ N(0, sigma^2)
u_i follows an iCAR ( model = "besag") correlation

I noticed that for some data sets I obtain a perfect fit (fitted values are identical to the observed data). I assume that the eps_i and u_i compete with each other? Would it be an option to set the sigma of eps_i to a very small value and keep it fixed? If I do this then the problem disappears. In WinBUGS you can put the CAR on the Y data (i.e. on eps_i)....

And a high ' Expected number of effective parameters' relative to the sample size......I assume that this means that I am overfitting the data? I guess that is linked to the problem described above.

Kind regards,

John

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] CAR
parts:
Hi John,

Is your likelihood Gaussian? And that is what you mean by eps_i? I assume so.

I suggest putting shrinkage priors on both effects, since the default prior is a bad choice! (We can't change the default because of backwards compatibility, so you should not use the default.)

See inla.doc('pc.prec')

How I do it, inside the INLA call, for the Gaussian likelihood:
  family = 'gaussian',
  control.family = list(hyper = list(prec = list(
              prior = "pc.prec", fixed = FALSE, param = c(sig.gauss.0,0.5)))),

Where I set sig.gauss.0 to a medium value, e.g. 0.5. If you want more shrinkage, set it to a small value, like 0.1.

You should do similar code in the besag random effect also, see the inla.doc.

Kind regards,
Haakon Bakka
